messages:
Anya R: heads up — bringing up ql-rerank-compact (int8) on devset showed a repeatable NDCG@10 drop vs float16. float16 0.392 -> int8 0.365 (~7% rel).
Leo K: ouch. same checkpoint, just quantized? any diffs in candidate ordering / preproc?
Anya R: same checkpoint, PTQ pipeline from bench-quant v2. Ran using eval harness v1.9. Quick check: MRR also down (0.278 -> 0.256).
Samir: can you paste the eval command you used? seed? sampling?
Anya R: ran the usual:
```bash
python run_eval.py --model ql-rerank-compact --dataset devset-v3 --batch 64 --quant int8 --seed 123
```
Anya R: sample size was smallish — N=500 queries (standard dev slice).
eval-bot: run 1849994321: finished. metrics: NDCG@10=0.365, MRR=0.256. logs: s3://redwood-evals/1849994321.log
Maya: could be candidate-ordering or tokenizer normalization. We saw a subtle jank before where the harness shuffles differently when batching is changed. Also check padding/truncation tokens.
Leo K: +1 to ordering. If the candidates got re-sorted by doc_id earlier in the pipeline the rank positions shift and NDCG can move a bunch on small queries.
Samir: let's do a reproducibility checklist: (1) preserve candidate ordering flag, (2) match tokenizer normalization exactly, (3) seed sweep 5 seeds, (4) bootstrap CI on N=1000 resamples.
Anya R: I just diffed harness v1.9 vs v1.8 — found a harmless-looking change that sorts JSON lines after loading (accidental). minimal patch: remove the sort. diff:
```diff
- data = sorted(load_jsonl(path), key=lambda x: x['doc_id'])
+ data = load_jsonl(path)  # preserve incoming order
```
Anya R: re-ran with preserve-order patch + seed 42: float16 0.391, int8 0.389 (now only ~0.5% diff). So ordering was the main culprit.
Maya: nice catch. That explains why smaller slices were sensitive. For completeness run Samir's bootstrap plan and a 5-seed sweep.
Samir: I'll kick off bootstrap + seeds on the cluster, gonna use 1000 resamples and seeds [1,42,123,999,2024]. I'll report back in this thread.
Leo K: also add a small test in harness CI to assert we don't reorder candidates unless explicitly requested.
Anya R: created PR with patch + unit test, linking in case folks want to review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/212
Samir: bootstrap job started (job id cb-9932). ETA ~18m.
Anya R: thanks everyone. follow-ups: Samir will post bootstrap CIs, Leo will add CI guard, Maya will double-check tokenizer parity in production pipeline. :thumbsup:
